annotation.title_clean: Ethical and Legal Challenges in the Use of Robotics for Critical Surgical Interventions
annotation.title_en: Ethical and Legal Challenges in the Use of Robotics for Critical Surgical Interventions
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Vashisht, N.; Goyal, W.; Choudhary, S.; Jayakumar, S.S.; Patil, S.; Mohapatra, C.K. et al.
annotation.venue: Seminars in Medical Writing and Education
annotation.summary_en: Journal article examining ethical and legal challenges of AI-driven robotic-assisted surgery: privacy, informed consent, algorithmic bias, liability for errors, unequal access due to cost. Reviews existing FDA/EMA-type frameworks as inadequate for autonomous surgical AI and recommends clearer liability rules, transparent AI, surgeon training and harmonised laws.
key_provisions_or_claims: Existing medical-device laws were designed for human surgery and do not cover AI-controlled surgical robots well.
Liability allocation among surgeons, manufacturers and AI developers remains unclear.
AI decision-making in surgery requires transparency and human oversight.
High cost of robotic systems creates inequitable access, especially in low-income countries.
Calls for surgeon training and harmonised legal frameworks and ethical standards.
